newsitem.title: INDIA: RBI abstains as India dlr demand rises, rupee flat.
newsitem.headline: RBI abstains as India dlr demand rises, rupee flat.

text.p: The rupee ended flat at 35.860/865 against the dollar in the spot market on Monday even as local demand for dollars spurted and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) abstained from dollar buying, dealers said.
"There was no need for RBI to intervene today (to arrest the rupee's rise) said the chief dealer at a private Bombay bank. Dealers at leading foreign banks confirmed RBI's abstention.
"The spurt in (dollar) demand was well-matched by supplies," said a dealer. The market has ben characterised in recent months by poor dollar demand against the backdrop of plentiful supplies.
The rupee strengthened in the forward market, forward premiums fell, largely reflecting the low overnight money market rates which closed at 0.10/0.25 percent on Monday.
The six month annualised premium closed at 6.47 percent compared to the previous close of 6.80 percent, dealers said.
"Forwards should drift downward with the (RBI's) repo cut-off having been lowered to 4.90 percent from 5.0 percent," a foreign bank said in its forex commentary on Monday morning.
"Till end April, most people appear covered," said a dealer, referring to near-term dollar requirement of corporates.
Some dealers said premiums are very low and set for a correction, with the rupee weakening on the forward market.
"I feel in a day or two the forward premiums should rise," said B. Manmadha Rao, manager (forex dealing) at the private Global Trust Bank Ltd in Bombay.
The foreign exchange market is inactive on Tuesday as banks in Bombay, the main commercial city, are closed for a holiday. Bombay banks resume operations on Wednesday.
